description: Parametric, multivariate, derived and data-driven probability distributions beyond the handful in the basic statistics chunk, plus the functions that interrogate any distribution object (survival and hazard functions, generating functions, domains, parameter assumptions).

tools.name: GammaDistribution
tools.description: Represents a gamma distribution with shape alpha and scale beta (mean alpha*beta). It models waiting times for alpha Poisson events and is the conjugate prior of Poisson/exponential rates; ExponentialDistribution and ErlangDistribution are special cases. The three- and four-argument forms give the generalized gamma family.
tools.usage:
GammaDistribution[alpha, beta]
GammaDistribution[alpha, beta, gamma, mu]
tools.notes: Wolfram parameterizes with scale beta, not rate; a rate-lambda gamma is GammaDistribution[alpha, 1/lambda]. ChiSquareDistribution[n] == GammaDistribution[n/2, 2].

tools.name: BetaDistribution
tools.description: Represents a continuous beta distribution on the interval (0,1) with shape parameters alpha and beta. It is the standard model for proportions and probabilities and the conjugate prior for Bernoulli/binomial success rates. Use with TransformedDistribution to rescale to another interval.
tools.example:
post = BetaDistribution[1 + 7, 1 + 3]; (* prior Beta(1,1), 7 successes, 3 failures *)
Mean[post]
Quantile[post, {0.025, 0.975}]
tools.notes: BetaDistribution[1, 1] is UniformDistribution[{0, 1}]. For matrix-valued or multivariate generalizations see DirichletDistribution.

tools.name: ChiSquareDistribution
tools.description: Represents a chi-squared distribution with nu degrees of freedom, the distribution of a sum of nu squared standard normals. It underlies goodness-of-fit tests, variance confidence intervals and likelihood-ratio statistics.
tools.example:
critical = InverseCDF[ChiSquareDistribution[4], 0.95]
1 - CDF[ChiSquareDistribution[4], 11.2] (* p-value of an observed statistic *)
tools.notes: Related: NoncentralChiSquareDistribution, ChiDistribution, InverseChiSquareDistribution.

tools.name: FRatioDistribution
tools.description: Represents the F distribution with n numerator and m denominator degrees of freedom, i.e. the ratio of two scaled chi-squared variables. It is the reference distribution for ANOVA and variance-ratio tests.
tools.notes: Named FRatioDistribution, not FDistribution. Mean exists only for m > 2.

tools.name: LogNormalDistribution
tools.description: Represents a log-normal distribution: Log[x] is normally distributed with mean mu and standard deviation sigma. Widely used for strictly positive, right-skewed quantities such as incomes, particle sizes and asset prices.

parameters.name: mu
parameters.description: Mean of the underlying normal (log scale).

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Standard deviation of the underlying normal, sigma > 0.

tools.notes: Mean is Exp[mu + sigma^2/2], not Exp[mu]; the median is Exp[mu].

tools.name: WeibullDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Weibull distribution with shape alpha and scale beta, the standard lifetime model in reliability engineering (alpha < 1 infant mortality, alpha = 1 exponential, alpha > 1 wear-out). A third argument adds a location shift.
tools.notes: Related lifetime models: ExponentialDistribution, GammaDistribution, FrechetDistribution, ReliabilityDistribution.

tools.name: CauchyDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Cauchy (Lorentzian) distribution with location a and scale b. It has undefined mean and variance and extremely heavy tails, making it a useful stress test for estimators and a model for resonance line shapes.
tools.notes: Equivalent to StudentTDistribution[1]. Use robust estimators (Median, MedianDeviation) with Cauchy data.

tools.name: LaplaceDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Laplace (double exponential) distribution with location mu and scale beta. It is the error distribution implied by least-absolute-deviation regression and the noise model in differential privacy.
tools.example:
PDF[LaplaceDistribution[0, 1], x]
RandomVariate[LaplaceDistribution[0, 1/epsilon]] (* Laplace mechanism noise *)
tools.notes: Variance is 2 beta^2.

tools.name: LogisticDistribution
tools.description: Represents a logistic distribution with location mu and scale beta, whose CDF is the logistic sigmoid. It is the latent-error distribution behind logistic regression and a heavier-tailed alternative to the normal.
tools.notes: Related: LogitModelFit, LogisticSigmoid.

tools.name: ParetoDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Pareto distribution with minimum value k and shape alpha; the two-, three- and four-argument forms give Pareto types I through IV. It models power-law tails such as wealth, city sizes and file sizes.
tools.usage:
ParetoDistribution[k, alpha]
ParetoDistribution[k, alpha, mu]
ParetoDistribution[k, alpha, gamma, mu]
tools.notes: Mean exists only for alpha > 1 and variance only for alpha > 2.

tools.name: GumbelDistribution
tools.description: Represents the Gumbel (type I extreme value, minimum form) distribution with location alpha and scale beta. Use it and ExtremeValueDistribution (maximum form) to model extreme events such as annual maximum floods or fatigue failures.
tools.example:
EstimatedDistribution[annualMinTemps, GumbelDistribution[a, b]]
ExtremeValueDistribution[a, b] (* maximum version *)
tools.notes: GumbelDistribution is the distribution of minima; ExtremeValueDistribution is the mirror image for maxima. See also FrechetDistribution and MaxStableDistribution.

tools.name: ExtremeValueDistribution
tools.description: Represents the type I extreme value distribution (Gumbel maximum form) with location alpha and scale beta, the limiting distribution of the maximum of many i.i.d. samples with exponential-like tails.
tools.example:
fit = EstimatedDistribution[annualMaxFlow, ExtremeValueDistribution[a, b]];
Quantile[fit, 1 - 1/100] (* 100-year return level *)
tools.notes: MaxStableDistribution generalizes it with a shape parameter (GEV family).

tools.name: RayleighDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Rayleigh distribution with scale sigma, the distribution of the magnitude of a 2D vector with independent normal components. It models wind speed, wave heights and fading amplitudes in wireless channels.
tools.notes: Special case of ChiDistribution with 2 degrees of freedom (scaled); RiceDistribution generalizes it with a non-zero mean.

tools.name: TriangularDistribution
tools.description: Represents a triangular distribution on {min, max} with optional mode c. It is a common subjective distribution in project-risk and Monte Carlo models when only the minimum, most-likely and maximum values are known.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Mode (peak), min <= c <= max; default is the midpoint.

tools.notes: Related: UniformDistribution, PERTDistribution for the beta-PERT variant.

tools.name: BernoulliDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Bernoulli distribution taking value 1 with probability p and 0 otherwise. It is the building block of binomial and geometric models and the natural output distribution for binary classifiers.
tools.notes: BinomialDistribution[1, p] is equivalent.

tools.name: GeometricDistribution
tools.description: Represents a geometric distribution with success probability p, giving the number of failures before the first success (support starting at 0). It is the discrete analogue of the exponential distribution and is memoryless.
tools.notes: Wolfram counts failures before the first success, so the support is {0, 1, 2, ...}; add 1 for the number of trials.

tools.name: NegativeBinomialDistribution
tools.description: Represents a negative binomial distribution: the number of failures before the n-th success with success probability p. It is the standard over-dispersed alternative to the Poisson distribution for count data.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of successes required, n > 0 (real values allowed).

tools.notes: For counts with variance > mean prefer this over PoissonDistribution; GeneralizedLinearModelFit does not support it directly.

tools.name: HypergeometricDistribution
tools.description: Represents a hypergeometric distribution: the number of successes in n draws without replacement from a population of size m_tot containing n_succ successes. Use it for sampling-inspection and lottery-type problems where draws are not independent.

parameters.name: nsucc
parameters.description: Number of successes in the population.

tools.example:
Probability[k >= 1, k \[Distributed] HypergeometricDistribution[5, 3, 50]]
(* P(at least one defective in 5 drawn from 50 with 3 defective) *)
tools.notes: Argument order is draws, successes, total. See MultivariateHypergeometricDistribution for several categories.

tools.name: DiscreteUniformDistribution
tools.description: Represents a uniform distribution on the integers from imin to imax. Use it for dice, random indices and any equally likely integer outcome.
tools.notes: RandomInteger[{1, 6}] is the quick way to sample; the distribution object is needed for symbolic work and Probability/Expectation.

tools.name: ZipfDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Zipf distribution with shape rho (and optional range n), a discrete power law used for word frequencies, city ranks and popularity data.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Optional maximum value for the finite version.

tools.notes: Related: BenfordDistribution for leading digits, ParetoDistribution for the continuous analogue.

tools.name: MultinormalDistribution
tools.description: Represents a multivariate normal distribution with mean vector mu and covariance matrix Sigma. It is the workhorse for correlated Gaussian noise, Kalman filtering, Gaussian processes and Bayesian linear models.
tools.notes: Sigma must be positive definite; use PositiveDefiniteMatrixQ to check. BinormalDistribution is the 2D special case parameterized by correlation.

tools.name: BinormalDistribution
tools.description: Represents a bivariate normal distribution with means, standard deviations and correlation rho. It is more convenient than MultinormalDistribution when the model is naturally expressed through a correlation coefficient.

tools.name: MultivariateTDistribution
tools.description: Represents a multivariate Student t distribution with scale matrix Sigma and nu degrees of freedom, a heavy-tailed alternative to the multinormal used in robust regression and finance.

tools.name: DirichletDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Dirichlet distribution with concentration parameters {alpha1, ..., alphak}, the multivariate generalization of the beta distribution over probability vectors. It is the conjugate prior of the multinomial and central to topic models and Bayesian categorical inference.
tools.notes: Samples have k-1 components in Wolfram's convention; the last coordinate is 1 minus their sum.

tools.name: MultinomialDistribution
tools.description: Represents a multinomial distribution for n trials with category probabilities {p1, ..., pk}, giving the joint distribution of the category counts. Use it for contingency tables, dice with several faces and categorical sampling.

tools.name: WishartMatrixDistribution
tools.description: Represents a Wishart distribution of random symmetric positive-definite matrices with nu degrees of freedom and scale matrix Sigma, the distribution of sample covariance matrices from multinormal data. Used in Bayesian covariance modelling and random matrix theory.
tools.notes: Related matrix distributions: InverseWishartMatrixDistribution, MatrixNormalDistribution, GaussianOrthogonalMatrixDistribution, CircularUnitaryMatrixDistribution.

tools.name: MixtureDistribution
tools.description: Represents a finite mixture of distributions with weights {w1, ..., wn}. Use it to model multimodal data such as populations composed of several subgroups; EstimatedDistribution can fit the weights and component parameters.

parameters.name: {dist1, ...}
parameters.description: Component distributions of the same dimension.

tools.notes: For a data-driven mixture use KernelMixtureDistribution or SmoothKernelDistribution; ParameterMixtureDistribution mixes over a continuous parameter.

tools.name: ParameterMixtureDistribution
tools.description: Represents a compound distribution in which a parameter of dist itself follows a distribution (e.g. Poisson with gamma-distributed rate gives the negative binomial). Use it for hierarchical / Bayesian marginal models.

parameters.name: dist
parameters.description: Distribution containing the symbolic parameter theta.

tools.name: TruncatedDistribution
tools.description: Represents dist restricted (and renormalized) to the interval {min, max}, or to a box for multivariate distributions. Use it when a physical quantity cannot leave a range, e.g. a normal distribution for a strictly positive measurement.
tools.usage:
TruncatedDistribution[{min, max}, dist]
TruncatedDistribution[{{min1, max1}, {min2, max2}}, dist]

parameters.name: {min, max}
parameters.description: Truncation bounds; use -Infinity or Infinity for one-sided truncation.

tools.notes: CensoredDistribution instead piles the outside mass onto the bounds.

tools.name: CensoredDistribution
tools.description: Represents dist censored to {min, max}: values outside the interval are reported as the boundary values rather than discarded. It models saturated sensors, detection limits and clipped measurements.
tools.notes: Compare TruncatedDistribution, which renormalizes instead of accumulating mass at the bounds.

tools.name: ProductDistribution
tools.description: Represents the joint distribution of independent components dist1, dist2, .... Use it to build multivariate distributions from independent marginals for Probability, Expectation and RandomVariate.
tools.notes: For dependent components use CopulaDistribution or MultinormalDistribution.

tools.name: CopulaDistribution
tools.description: Represents a multivariate distribution with given marginals joined by a copula kernel such as "Product", "Frank", "Clayton", "GumbelHougaard", "FGM", {"Binormal", rho} or {"Multinormal", Sigma}. It separates the dependence structure from the marginal shapes, as used in risk aggregation and finance.

parameters.name: ker
parameters.description: Copula kernel specification, e.g. {"Clayton", alpha} or {"Binormal", rho}.

tools.name: MarginalDistribution
tools.description: Extracts the marginal distribution of one or several components of a multivariate distribution. Use it to inspect individual variables of a joint model without integrating by hand.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Component index or list of indices to keep.

tools.name: OrderDistribution
tools.description: Represents the distribution of the k-th order statistic (k-th smallest value) in a sample of size n from dist. Use it for minima, maxima, medians and record values.
tools.usage:
OrderDistribution[{dist, n}, k]
OrderDistribution[{dist, n}, {k1, k2, ...}]

tools.name: KernelMixtureDistribution
tools.description: Builds a kernel density estimate as a genuine distribution object (a mixture of kernels centred on the data points) that supports PDF, CDF, RandomVariate, Expectation and plotting. Use it for nonparametric density modelling of continuous data.
tools.usage:
KernelMixtureDistribution[data]
KernelMixtureDistribution[data, bw]
KernelMixtureDistribution[data, bw, ker]

parameters.name: bw
parameters.description: Bandwidth, or a rule such as "Silverman", "Scott", "LeastSquaresCrossValidation".

tools.notes: SmoothKernelDistribution is the same idea implemented as an interpolated density; KernelMixtureDistribution is exact but slower for large data.

tools.name: HistogramDistribution
tools.description: Creates a piecewise-constant probability distribution from binned data, i.e. a histogram usable as a distribution object. Use it as a quick nonparametric model or to resample from an empirical density.

parameters.name: bspec
parameters.description: Bin specification: bin width, {min, max, dx}, number of bins, or a rule like "Scott".

tools.notes: EmpiricalDistribution gives point masses at the data values instead of a piecewise-uniform density.

tools.name: SurvivalFunction
tools.description: Gives the survival function S(x) = 1 - CDF[dist, x] of a distribution, i.e. the probability of exceeding x. Fundamental in reliability and survival analysis; also available as a property of SurvivalModelFit results.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Evaluation point; omit to get a pure function.

tools.name: HazardFunction
tools.description: Gives the hazard (failure-rate) function PDF/Survival of a distribution, the instantaneous rate of failure given survival to x. Constant for the exponential distribution, increasing for Weibull with shape > 1.
tools.example:
HazardFunction[WeibullDistribution[a, b], t] // Simplify
HazardFunction[ExponentialDistribution[lambda], t] (* lambda *)

tools.name: CharacteristicFunction
tools.description: Gives the characteristic function E[Exp[I t X]] of a distribution as a symbolic expression in t. Useful for proving convolution results, inverting to densities and analysing stable laws.
tools.notes: MomentGeneratingFunction and CumulantGeneratingFunction are the real-argument analogues.

tools.name: MomentGeneratingFunction
tools.description: Gives the moment generating function E[Exp[t X]] of a distribution. Differentiating at t = 0 yields raw moments; the function may not exist for heavy-tailed distributions.
tools.example:
mgf = MomentGeneratingFunction[GammaDistribution[a, b], t]
D[mgf, {t, 2}] /. t -> 0 (* second raw moment *)
tools.notes: See also CumulantGeneratingFunction, Cumulant, FactorialMoment and FactorialMomentGeneratingFunction.

tools.name: DistributionDomain
tools.description: Gives the support of a distribution as an Interval (continuous) or Range/Integers specification (discrete). Use it to determine integration or summation limits and to validate values before evaluating PDF.

tools.name: DistributionParameterAssumptions
tools.description: Gives the conditions the symbolic parameters of a distribution must satisfy for it to be valid (e.g. sigma > 0). Use it with Assuming, Refine or Simplify when deriving results with symbolic parameters, and DistributionParameterQ to test concrete values.

parameters.name: dist
parameters.description: Distribution with symbolic or numeric parameters.

tools.example:
DistributionParameterAssumptions[GammaDistribution[a, b]] (* a > 0 && b > 0 *)
Assuming[DistributionParameterAssumptions[NormalDistribution[m, s]], Simplify[Variance[NormalDistribution[m, s]]]]
DistributionParameterQ[NormalDistribution[0, -1]] (* False *)

tools.name: ReliabilityDistribution
tools.description: Builds the lifetime distribution of a system from a Boolean structure function of component lifetimes (series = And, parallel = Or, k-out-of-n via BooleanCountingFunction) and the component distributions. Use it for system reliability, MTTF and survival curves of redundant designs.

parameters.name: bexpr
parameters.description: Boolean expression in the component symbols that is True when the system works.

parameters.name: {{x1, dist1}, ...}
parameters.description: Component symbols and their lifetime distributions.

tools.notes: FailureDistribution takes the complementary formulation (expression true when the system fails). StandbyDistribution models cold/warm standby.
